plurals.name: resume_message
plurals.item: Deja stopped part way through and has %d screenshot read so far. It can carry on from there, or forget those and read everything again.
Deja stopped part way through and has %d screenshots read so far. It can carry on from there, or forget those and read everything again.

resources.string: You\'ve already seen it.\nNow you can find it.
Deja reads your screenshots so you can search them in words instead of scrolling for them. To do that it needs to see your Screenshots folder.
Android won\'t show the permission prompt again after it has been declined, so it has to be switched on by hand. Open Settings → Permissions → Photos and videos, and choose Allow all.
Reading happens entirely on this phone. Deja has no internet permission at all, so nothing it reads can be sent anywhere.
Already granted it? Come back and Deja will pick it up.
Android is blocking Deja\'s notifications, so it can\'t tell you what\'s in a new screenshot. You can allow them in Settings.

Writes everything Deja has read to a JSON file you choose. One-time codes, passwords, and card and ID numbers are left out — including where they appear in the text — unless you choose to include them.
Starting over throws that progress away and reads everything again.
Clearing the index now stops the scan and forgets what it has read so far.

plurals.name: privacy_forget_message
plurals.item: This clears the index of %d screenshot. The screenshot itself stays exactly where it is — Deja would just have to read it again.
This clears the index of %d screenshots. The screenshots themselves stay exactly where they are — Deja would just have to read them again.

resources.string: Not a policy you have to trust — a permission the app was never given. It cannot send your screenshots anywhere.
Every model runs on this device
No account, no sign-in, no cloud backup
No analytics and no crash reporting
ID and card numbers stay masked until tapped
Tell me what\'s in a new screenshot
Take a screenshot of a code, a Wi-Fi password, a booking or a payment and Deja shows it in a notification with Copy. Read on this phone like everything else; codes stay masked.
Deja can only see the screenshots you picked
Android 14 lets you grant a hand-picked set. Tap to choose more, or allow the whole folder.
Keeps everything read so far. You can resume later.
The last scan stopped before it finished. This picks up where it left off.
Scan for screenshots taken or removed since last time
Everything Deja has read, as a file you keep. There is nowhere else it could be.
Clears the index. Your screenshots themselves stay put.
Because Deja can\'t go online, we can\'t see how you use it. If something breaks, please tell us — we\'re flying blind on purpose.
Deja collects nothing at all, so a message from you is genuinely the only way we hear about a problem.
You\'ve already seen it. Now you can find it.
Read from the filename. Some phones don\'t record the app, so this won\'t cover everything.
Deja has no ads, no accounts and no tracking. This is the whole business model.
WhatsApp or email — whichever suits you
Emails us the crash log Deja kept on this phone. You see it before it goes.
Emails us your phone model and Android version, and whatever you write.
Ratings are how people find an app that can\'t advertise itself.

Deja reads the text in each screenshot on your phone and keeps a private index of it, so you can find things by what they say. Reading is done by an on-device model bundled inside the app — nothing is uploaded and nothing is downloaded. It only reads screenshots it hasn\'t seen before, so a full pass is a one-time cost rather than something that happens every launch.
